title: Field-extension lifting calculus for families of presheaves
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with presheaves of sets on schemes over $S$, with test schemes and universes as in [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-size-convention]. Joint surjectivity means the field-extension lifting condition of [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]: every section over $(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)$, for a field $K$ [def-weil-field] and a map $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, lifts to some member of the family after a field embedding $K\to L$. (1) For an isomorphism $e:G\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ of presheaves, the singleton family $\{e\}$ is jointly surjective. (2) Let $I$ be a set and $J_i$ a set for each $i\in I$. Let $F,G_i,H_{ij}$ be presheaves, with natural transformations $f_i:G_i\to F$ and $g_{ij}:H_{ij}\to G_i$. If $(f_i)_{i\in I}$ is jointly surjective and $(g_{ij})_{j\in J_i}$ is jointly surjective for every $i$, then $(f_i\circ g_{ij})_{(i,j)\in\coprod_{i\in I}J_i}$ is jointly surjective. (3) Let $(f_i:G_i\to F)_{i\in I}$ be jointly surjective and let $a:F'\to F$ be any natural transformation of presheaves. Define $P_i$ objectwise by $P_i(T)=\{(x',y)\in F'(T)\times G_i(T)\mid a_T(x')=(f_i)_T(y)\}$, with restriction of pairs. Then the first projections $(P_i\to F')_{i\in I}$ are jointly surjective. Empty index sets are allowed. No etaleness or representability of the natural transformations, and no sheaf hypothesis, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), the point-surjectivity arguments in parts (1)-(3), separated from the etale condition and stated for presheaves. Field-valued point conventions: spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU (definition-points) and its preceding paragraph. Extracts returned steps 9,10.

proof.text: For clause (1), fix a field $K$, an $S$-structure $s$ and $x\in F(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)$. Evaluate the inverse natural transformation to obtain $y=(e^{-1})_{(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)}(x)\in G(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)$. The inverse identity evaluated at $x$ gives $e(y)=x$. Choose the sole family index, $L=K$ and the identity embedding $K\to K$. Restriction along this embedding is the identity by the presheaf identity axiom. These data satisfy the lifting definition, proving (1).

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), omitted proof of (1)-(3); field-valued representatives as in spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU (definition-points) and the preceding paragraph.

proof.text: For clause (2), fix $K,s,x$ as in the lifting definition. Apply that definition to $(f_i)$ to obtain $i$, an embedding $u:K\to L$, and $y\in G_i(\operatorname{Spec}L,s_L)$ with $f_i(y)=x|_L$, where $s_L=s\circ\operatorname{Spec}u$. Apply it again to $(g_{ij})_j$ over this same $S$-structured field $L$, to obtain $j\in J_i$, an embedding $v:L\to M$, and $z\in H_{ij}(\operatorname{Spec}M,s_M)$ with $g_{ij}(z)=y|_M$. The composite $v\circ u$ is an embedding since both maps are injective ring homomorphisms. The map of spectra for the composite is the composite in the reverse order, so $s_M=s_L\circ\operatorname{Spec}v=s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(v\circ u)$. Naturality of $f_i$ and the presheaf composition axiom give $(f_i\circ g_{ij})_M(z)=(f_i)_M(y|_M)=f_i(y)|_M=(x|_L)|_M=x|_M$. Thus $(i,j)$, $M$, $v\circ u$, and $z$ are the required witnesses. The two successive witness fields remain in the fixed universe; no simultaneous extension or enlargement is used.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), omitted proof of (1)-(3); field-valued representatives as in spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU (definition-points) and the preceding paragraph.

proof.text: For clause (3), first check that the displayed objectwise formula defines a presheaf and its projection defines a natural transformation. For an $S$-morphism $r:T_1\to T_0$ and $(x',y)\in P_i(T_0)$, naturality gives $a_{T_1}(x'|_r)=a_{T_0}(x')|_r=(f_i)_{T_0}(y)|_r=(f_i)_{T_1}(y|_r)$. Hence restriction sends the pair to $(x'|_r,y|_r)\in P_i(T_1)$. Identity and composite restriction agree coordinatewise because they do so in $F'$ and $G_i$; equality of pairs with their compatibility proofs reduces to equality of the coordinates. First projection commutes with restriction since both orders return $x'|_r$. The sets of compatible pairs are subsets of the indicated products in the chosen universe.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), omitted proof of (1)-(3); field-valued representatives as in spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU (definition-points) and the preceding paragraph.

proof.text: Now fix a field $K$, $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, and $x'\in F'(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)$. Apply the lifting definition for $(f_i)$ to $a_K(x')\in F(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)$. Obtain $i$, an embedding $u:K\to L$, and $y\in G_i(\operatorname{Spec}L,s_L)$ with $(f_i)_L(y)=a_K(x')|_L$. Naturality of $a$ identifies the last expression with $a_L(x'|_L)$. Thus $(x'|_L,y)$ is an element of precisely the set $P_i(\operatorname{Spec}L,s_L)$ defined in the statement, and its first projection is $x'|_L$. These are the witnesses required for joint surjectivity of $(P_i\to F')$, proving (3).

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), omitted proof of (1)-(3); field-valued representatives as in spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BU (definition-points) and the preceding paragraph.

proof.text: The arguments respect empty families. By the lifting definition the empty family into $F$ is jointly surjective exactly when $F(\operatorname{Spec}K,s)$ is empty for every $K,s$: a section would require an index in the empty set, and in the absence of sections the condition is vacuous. In (2), if $I$ is empty there is therefore no $x$ to lift. If a particular $J_i$ is empty, joint surjectivity of that inner family forces $G_i$ to have no field-valued sections, so the outer lift cannot choose such an $i$ together with $y$. In (3), if $I$ is empty, any $x'$ would yield the impossible section $a_K(x')$ of $F$; hence the conclusion for the empty base-changed family is vacuous as well. No step assumes that $S$ has a field-valued point, so the empty base scheme is also included.

lean.statement: theorem presheaf_field_lift_family_calculus (S : Scheme.{u}) : (∀ (F G : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (e : G ≅ F), IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ e.hom)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type v) (J : I → Type w) (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (G : I → (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (H : ∀ i : I, J i → (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : ∀ i : I, G i ⟶ F) (g : ∀ (i : I) (j : J i), H i j ⟶ G i), IsJointlySurjective f → (∀ i : I, IsJointlySurjective (g i)) → IsJointlySurjective (fun ij : Sigma J ↦ g ij.1 ij.2 ≫ f ij.1)) ∧ (∀ (I : Type v) (F F' : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (G : I → (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : ∀ i : I, G i ⟶ F) (a : F' ⟶ F), IsJointlySurjective f → IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (PullbackCone.combine a (f i) (fun T ↦ Types.pullbackCone (a.app T) ((f i).app T)) (fun T ↦ (Types.pullbackLimitCone (a.app T) ((f i).app T)).isLimit)).fst))
